steps.tx: Gastrointestinal digestive function is orchestrated by specialized peptide hormones secreted by enteroendocrine cells dispersed throughout mucosal epithelium. The classical gastrin-cholecystokinin family is characterized by identical C-terminal pentapeptide amide sequences that bind distinct G-protein coupled **CCK receptor subtypes** with differing anatomical and organ distributions.
steps.say: Gastrin and CCK share an identical five-amino-acid end sequence, binding distinct G-protein coupled receptors.

left.title: CCK-A (Alimentary) Receptor
points: Expressed predominantly on gallbladder smooth muscle and pancreatic acini
Binds sulfated cholecystokinin with 1000-fold higher affinity than gastrin
Coupled to Gq proteins, activating phospholipase C and IP3/Ca2+
Mediates gallbladder contraction and pancreatic enzyme exocytosis

right.title: CCK-B (Brain / Gastric) Receptor
points: Expressed on gastric parietal cells, ECL cells, and central neurons
Binds gastrin and cholecystokinin with equal, high affinity
Coupled to Gq proteins, elevating intracellular calcium
Mediates gastric acid secretion and mucosal trophic growth

steps.tx: Synthesized and secreted by G cells located predominantly in the gastric antrum and proximal duodenum, the peptide hormone **gastrin** exists in two principal circulating molecular forms: big gastrin (G-34) and little gastrin (G-17). Both forms stimulate parietal cell acid output and exert potent trophic effects on gastric mucosa.
steps.say: Gastrin is secreted by antral G cells in two main forms, stimulating acid secretion and mucosal cell proliferation.

left.title: Little Gastrin (G-17)
points: Composed of 17 amino acids; produced primarily by antral G cells
Shorter biological half-life (~7 minutes in circulation)
Principal form secreted acutely in response to meal ingestion
Potent acute stimulant of parietal cell hydrochloric acid secretion

right.title: Big Gastrin (G-34)
points: Composed of 34 amino acids; synthesized by duodenal enteroendocrine cells
Significantly longer biological half-life (~35 to 40 minutes)
Predominant circulating form during interdigestive basal fasting state
Provides sustained background trophic signaling to gastric mucosa

steps.tx: Stimuli triggering antral gastrin exocytosis include luminal amino acids (particularly aromatic phenylalanine and tryptophan), gastric distension via vagal gastrin-releasing peptide, and physiological hypercalcemia. Conversely, when luminal gastric pH falls below two, antral D cells release somatostatin, initiating **paracrine gastrin inhibition**.
steps.say: Digested aromatic amino acids and vagal GRP stimulate gastrin release, while luminal acidity shuts it down via somatostatin.

nodes.label: Ingested Peptides and Phenylalanine Stimulate Apical Antral G Cell Receptors
Vagal Efferents Release Gastrin-Releasing Peptide (GRP / Bombesin)
G Cells Secrete Gastrin into Antral Venous Capillaries
Gastrin Stimulates ECL Histamine and Parietal CCK-B Receptors to Drive Acid Output

steps.tx: Uncontrolled, autonomous hypersecretion of gastrin by a neuroendocrine gastrinoma (most commonly in the duodenum or pancreas) causes **Zollinger-Ellison syndrome**. Massive hypergastrinaemia induces hypertrophy of gastric fundic folds and unrelenting hyperchlorhydria, resulting in multiple refractory peptic ulcerations, severe gastroesophageal reflux, and malabsorptive diarrhea.
steps.say: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome is a gastrinoma producing severe hypergastrinaemia, hypertrophic rugae, and refractory peptic ulcers.

steps.tx: Synthesized by I cells in the duodenum and jejunum, **cholecystokinin** is released in response to luminal monoglycerides, free fatty acids, and intact oligopeptides. CCK coordinates upper gastrointestinal digestion by contracting the gallbladder, stimulating pancreatic enzyme secretion, and delaying gastric emptying to allow thorough duodenal digestion.
steps.say: Cholecystokinin is secreted by I cells in response to fat and protein, contracting the gallbladder and slowing gastric emptying.

rows: Permits free bile and pancreatic entry into duodenum

steps.tx: Historically known as nature's antacid, the peptide hormone **secretin** is synthesized by S cells situated within the crypts of Lieberkühn of the duodenum. Secretin is released when acidic gastric chyme containing free protons drops duodenal intraluminal pH below four point five.
steps.say: Secretin is nature's antacid, released by duodenal S cells whenever acidic chyme drops pH below four point five.

nodes.label: Acidic Gastric Chyme (pH < 4.5) Empties Through Pylorus into Duodenum
Duodenal S Cells Sense Protons and Secrete Peptide Secretin into Blood
Secretin Binds Ductal Cells in Pancreas and Biliary Cholangiocytes
Massive Ductal Bicarbonate Secretion Neutralizes Duodenal pH to ~7.0-8.0

steps.tx: Secretin acts via cyclic AMP on pancreatic and biliary ductal cells to stimulate profuse aqueous bicarbonate secretion, neutralizing gastric hydrochloric acid. Simultaneously, secretin inhibits **gastric acid secretion** by stimulating antral somatostatin release and promoting pyloric sphincter closure, shielding the delicate duodenal mucosa from peptic ulceration.
steps.say: Secretin stimulates ductal bicarbonate output while inhibiting gastric acid production to protect duodenal mucosa.

left.title: Cholecystokinin (CCK)
points: Secreted by duodenal and jejunal I cells
Primary trigger: Luminal fat (fatty acids >8 carbons) and peptides
Acts via Gq protein, IP3, and intracellular calcium
Stimulates pancreatic acinar enzyme exocytosis

right.title: Secretin
points: Secreted by duodenal S cells in crypts of Lieberkühn
Primary trigger: Acidic luminal chyme with pH below 4.5
Acts via Gs protein, adenylyl cyclase, and cyclic AMP
Stimulates pancreatic and biliary ductal bicarbonate secretion

steps.tx: A hormone test can interrogate a gastrinoma by asking what its cells obey. The **secretin stimulation test** exploits a paradox: secretin suppresses normal antral gastrin but provokes a sharp rise from gastrinoma tissue, so a rising level after injection supports the tumour. It separates Zollinger Ellison physiology from ordinary acid hypersecretion causes. Like many endocrine tests, its meaning lives entirely in the direction of change, not in any single value.
steps.say: Secretin lowers normal gastrin but raises gastrinoma output, so a paradoxical rise diagnoses Zollinger Ellison physiology. Direction of change is the test.

vis.alt: Image showing the secretin stimulation test with gastrin rising in gastrinoma.
vis.caption: Gastrin lines diverge after secretin, rising only in the gastrinoma patient. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: In clinical gastroenterology, the **secretin stimulation test** serves as the gold standard for diagnosing early chronic pancreatitis and distinguishing gastrinomas. In Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, intravenous secretin paradoxically triggers a dramatic surge in circulating gastrin exceeding one hundred twenty picograms per millilitre, whereas normal G cells are suppressed.
steps.say: The secretin test paradoxically spikes gastrin in Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, while testing ductal bicarbonate in pancreatitis.
